summary: Ran genuine counter-evidence searches against all 8 target claims from counter-evidence-plan.md across 3 rounds. Strongest counter-evidence found for C1 (job-board segment mismatch — Faith Communities Today and Lifeway Research independent data confirm 70% of US churches are small enough to plausibly lack a paid small-group role) and C3 (SmartGroups free tier — the app's own App Store listing shows only 15 ratings despite marketing framing, plus cross-domain freemium conversion benchmarks). Moderate counter-evidence found for C2 (faith.tools — independent Similarweb traffic data shows low, declining volume and a small newsletter audience), C4 (EdTech champion analogy — volunteer-motivation and church-volunteer-turnover literature complicates the paid-staff-champion transfer), C6 (screen-free posture — Barna 2026 survey and a faith-media rebuttal piece support a minority-position framing), and C8 (vendor scale numbers — no independent verification exists, and secondary sources describing ChurchTrac's user count are inconsistent, while independent ChMS market-size estimates vary by over 4x). C5 (another-app fatigue) produced a genuine complication (Barna/Pushpay 2026 data skews positive on tech sentiment) but stays moderate-confidence since the source is vendor-sponsored. C7 (Sept/Jan timing) yielded an honest absence: no tool/vendor-pitch-specific timing source was found even among newer (2023-2025) material, so it is reported as an unresolved scope gap per the plan's own guidance rather than treated as either confirmed or refuted. All 8 claims received a good-faith, source-tier-labeled counter-evidence attempt; none were rubber-stamped or skipped.
